decision: Removed automatic Browserbase retries after network exceptions
why: A thrown fetch cannot establish that a paid Search or Fetch request was never accepted, so replay could duplicate cost or side effects
result: VERIFIED one request on ambiguous failure

decision: Applied one HTTP and HTTPS URL schema to Sail tool arguments, Browserbase results, and public Fleet events
why: Generic URL validation accepts file, FTP, and mail schemes that research tools must never fetch
result: VERIFIED unsupported schemes fail before provider calls

decision: Clarified that Sail model turns are synchronous while the coordinator remains outside the HTTP request lifecycle
why: Live verification superseded the earlier shorthand that called Sail workers asynchronous
result: prior grounding retained; runtime boundary corrected

decision: Added a sanitized, reproducible record for the three-worker live-provider run
why: Raw provider responses and ignored SQLite state are not suitable repository evidence
result: live result and Gateway verification gap recorded

decision: Extended the shared web URL boundary to reject literal loopback, private-network, link-local, and IPv6 targets
why: HTTP and HTTPS scheme checks alone still admit non-public destinations
result: local targets fail before provider calls

decision: Normalized trailing DNS dots before public-host checks
why: Fully qualified localhost with a trailing dot resolves to loopback but bypasses an exact hostname comparison
result: localhost and localhost-dot fail before provider calls

decision: Added resolved-address validation and disabled Browserbase redirects
why: Lexical hostname checks cannot detect metadata aliases, private DNS answers, or public-to-private redirects
result: all resolved addresses must be public before one non-redirecting Fetch call

decision: Repeated the live-worker path after DNS enforcement
why: Security controls must preserve the intended Sail plus Browserbase workflow
result: VERIFIED one worker, one Search, three Fetch calls, and synthesis completed

decision: Replaced hand-written IP range checks with ipaddr.js range classification
why: IPv4-mapped IPv6 has multiple canonical forms and denylist parsing missed hexadecimal private addresses
result: mapped loopback, private, and link-local forms classify as non-public
